To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a novel 3-D co-culture model was developed to study cell-cell interaction between osteobalsts and chondroycytes, and 2) co-culturing of osteobalsts with chondrocyts resulted in decreased GAG deposition and cell-mediated mineralization, but maintained osteoblast phenotype in vitro.

co-culture of chondrocyte and osteoblast in 3-D alginate scaffolds modulates cell phenotypic expression, and the interaction between these cell types may be important in osteochondral interface tissue engineering.

co-culture of osteoprogenitor cells and chondroprogenitor cells in 3-D hydrogel culture results in a significant decrease in chondrogenic differentiation of chondroprogentior cells and a significant decrease in osteogenic differentiation of osteoprogenior cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a tissue-engineered osteo-chondral graft that is capable of restoring a functional osteochondral interface in the knee.
the development of novel strategies for the regeneration of osteochondral tissue defects.
developing a better understanding of the cellular and molecular interactions that occur at the osteochondral junction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this model is a useful tool for the evaluation of the interaction between osteoblastic and chondroblastic cells in the regeneration of the osteochondral junction.
co-culture of osteo- and chondroblasts modulates cellular differentiation, and the effects of these interactions on tissue-engineered grafts will be investigated.
the co-culture of osteoprogenitor cells and chondroprogenitor cells is a promising approach in tissue engineering of the osteochondral unit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel co-culture model for studying osteochondral interface formation.
co-culturing chondrocyte with osteoblasts in 3-D scaffolds is a useful model to study the interaction between these two types of cells.

the sequential co-cultures of osteoblast and cartilage chondrocyte cells can be maintained in vitro for 6 weeks and that the co-cultured cells can produce a cartilage-like matrix and an osteoid-like matrix.
The main takeaway from our work is that
co-culture of osteochondral cells in a 3-D scaffold system can be used to study the interaction between these cells and how they modulate the phenotype of one another.
co-culture of osteogenic and chondrogenic cells in 3-D scaffolds can be used as an effective tool to study osteochondral regeneration in vitro.
the co-culture of osteochondral progenitors can modulate cell differentiation in vitro.
